transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yes, thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up time for someone who needs it more, but... um... I suppose what finally made me realize I should probably say something to someone is that... well, lately, after I eat a bit too much, I've been going upstairs and... making myself sick. Throwing up. 

And then I just come back down and act as if I was just tidying the kitchen or getting ready for bed, so nobody notices. It sounds terrible when I say it out loud, doesn't it? I just... I wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing by coming in to talk to you about it. Is that okay?
Can you tell me how you feel about your body weight or shape? Does it concern you a lot?

Well... um, I suppose it does concern me, yes. Probably more than it should. It's a bit silly, really. My daughter—and actually, a very sweet woman from my church—they've both told me recently that they think I look too thin. And I know they're just looking out for me, I really do. 

But... oh, it's so embarrassing to admit this out loud... if I'm getting dressed for work and my skirt feels even slightly snug, or if I see the scale has gone up by just a single pound, I get this... this awful panic. It's as if I feel I've somehow let myself become huge overnight, even though logically I know that's not possible. 

Does that make any sense? I know I shouldn't be so focused on it at my age, and I feel quite foolish even bringing it up. I hope I'm answering your question okay... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Can you tell me if you've ever had episodes where you feel like you're eating an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time, and feel like you can't stop or control how much you eat during those times?

Oh... well... I suppose... yes. I wouldn't say I completely lose my mind, but... I do have moments where I get a bit carried away. I hope you don't think terribly of me for saying this, it's just so embarrassing. 

Sometimes, when my husband is in the other room and no one is in the kitchen with me, I might start just picking at things. And then, before I really realize what I'm doing, I can go through all the leftovers from a church supper... and then I'll have crackers, and cheese, and cookies. Sometimes I'll even eat whatever I just baked for my book club, all in one sitting. 

It's far, far more than I would ever actually serve myself if I were sitting down to a proper meal. I feel dreadful even admitting it to you. Is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the answers you need.
Do you usually make yourself sick after these episodes of eating a lot, or do you sometimes do it even when you haven’t eaten that much?

Well, um... yes, like I mentioned when we first sat down—and I still feel just awful even repeating it—it's really just after those times when I eat too much. That's actually what finally made me realize I needed to say something and come see you. After I get carried away with the food, I'll... I'll go upstairs and make myself throw up. 

And then, like I said, I just come back down and act as if I was just tidying the kitchen or getting ready for bed, so my husband doesn't suspect anything is wrong. I don't really do it if I've just had a normal, small meal... at least, I don't think so. It's mostly just when I feel I've overdone it and I need to fix it. Is... is that helpful? I hope I'm explaining it properly for you.
Besides making yourself sick after eating, do you ever fast, exercise excessively, or use laxatives or diuretics to try to control your weight?

Oh, no, I don't use laxatives or water pills or anything like that. That always seemed a bit too... well, a bit extreme, I suppose. 

But, um... as for the other things you mentioned... I suppose I do try to make up for it a little bit. I hope you don't think I'm completely foolish for doing this. Sometimes, the next day, I'll just... skip breakfast and lunch. I usually just tell my coworkers at the dispensary that I had a big meal the night before and I'm just not hungry, but really it's just to try and balance things out. 

And I do walk with a group of ladies from my neighborhood, and I might... well, I might push myself to do a few extra laps. It's not because I'm feeling particularly energetic or anything, it's really just because I'm trying to undo what I ate. 

I know it's probably not the right way to handle things, and I feel a bit silly admitting it. I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details... is that the sort of thing you needed to know?
How often do these episodes of eating a lot and then making yourself sick happen? Do they happen regularly, like at least once a week or more often?

Oh, dear... well... I really want to be completely honest with you, even though it's just so hard to say out loud. I don't want it to sound like I'm completely out of control, because I really do try my best to keep things together... but... 

Well, I suppose if I'm looking back... ever since last winter, there has hardly been a week when I haven't had at least one of those... private eating spells. And then, of course, I feel so awful about it that I end up trying to make up for it, just like we talked about—by throwing up, or skipping my meals at the dispensary, or overdoing my walking with the ladies. 

I know that probably sounds dreadful, having it happen at least once a week for that long. I hope you don't think less of me for letting it get to this point, I really am trying. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the exact information you're looking for. Is that the timeline you needed to know?
Do you make yourself sick or try to compensate for eating even when you don’t feel like you’ve eaten too much, or is it always connected to times when you feel you’ve overeaten?

Oh, um... well, I think I might have touched on this a little bit when we first started talking, but I am more than happy to clarify, of course. It's... it's really just connected to the times when I feel I've eaten far too much. 

If I just have a sensible lunch at work or a regular, small dinner with my husband, I don't... I don't do anything like that. I really do try to be quite normal most of the time. It's truly only when I have one of those awful spells where I get completely carried away that I feel I absolutely have to undo it. 

I hope that makes sense? I really don't want you to think I'm just doing this after every little thing I eat... I'm trying my best to give you the exact right picture so you can help me. Did I explain that alright?

Can you tell me if the urge to make yourself sick or compensate with fasting or extra walking only happens after you feel you've eaten a lot, or if sometimes you do it even when you haven’t eaten more than usual?

Oh, um... well, I know I just mentioned this, but I'm so sorry if I wasn't clear enough. I really do want to be helpful. 

It's... it's only ever after I've had one of those times where I eat far too much. Truly. If I just have a normal meal, I don't feel that urge at all. I really try to be quite sensible the rest of the time. It's just when I lose control and eat a large amount that I feel I have to... well, fix it, I suppose. 

I hope I'm answering your question properly? I just don't want you to think I'm completely unreasonable or doing this all the time. Is that what you needed to know?
When you make yourself sick after eating, is it mainly because you're afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if others might tell you you're already thin?

Oh, goodness... well, yes. I suppose that really is the heart of it, isn't it? I know it probably sounds a bit silly, or perhaps a little vain, for a woman my age to be quite so preoccupied with her figure. I really try not to be superficial, I promise... but... yes, I am terribly afraid of gaining weight. 

It's actually quite confusing sometimes, because my daughter—and even a lovely woman from my church—have both recently told me that they think I look a bit too thin. They mean well, of course. But I just... I can't seem to see what they see. If my work skirt feels even the slightest bit snug when I put it on, or if I step on the scale and it's up even just a single pound... I just absolutely panic. It feels as if I've somehow let myself become completely huge overnight. 

I know that's probably not a very rational way to think, and I really do try to talk myself out of it when it happens. I hope you don't think I'm completely foolish for letting something like a pound on the scale frighten me so much... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the honest truth. Is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
